text: Photography is an art form that captures moments in time, transforming the world around us into a work of art. The act of taking a photograph involves several key elements: the shutter, which controls the time the camera's lens is open, and the aperture, which regulates the amount of light entering the camera. When a shutter is open, it exposes the image to light, while the aperture determines the amount of light that enters. The aperture is typically adjusted by a lens cap or a shutter release, allowing for precise control over the light entering the camera. This is achieved by opening or closing the aperture, thus altering the light that is allowed to enter. Shutter speeds range from very fast (such as 1/1000th of a second) to very slow (such as 1/8000th of a second), depending on the desired effect and the type of subject being photographed.
